summaries.baseline:
**Manchester City Clinch Convincing Victory Over Fluminense in Club World Cup Opener**

In a commanding display at King Abdullah Sports City, Manchester City cruised to a 4-0 victory over Brazilian side Fluminense in their FIFA Club World Cup 2024 opener. The English champions showcased their attacking prowess and tactical superiority, leaving no room for doubt about their intentions in the prestigious tournament.

City opened the scoring early, with a well-timed strike from Erling Haaland in the 12th minute, setting the tone for the rest of the match. The Norwegian forward, known for his clinical finishing, capitalized on a pinpoint cross from Kevin De Bruyne, who orchestrated much of City's attacking play.

Fluminense struggled to find their rhythm against the relentless pressure from Pep Guardiola's side. City doubled their lead just before halftime, courtesy of a deft finish from Phil Foden, who latched onto a clever through ball from Bernardo Silva.

The second half saw more of the same as Manchester City continued to dominate possession and create chances. Riyad Mahrez added a third goal in the 62nd minute, curling a sublime shot into the top corner after a dazzling solo run. The Brazilian outfit's defense was left in disarray, unable to contain City's fluid movement and quick passing.

The final nail in the coffin came in the 78th minute when substitute Julian Alvarez found the back of the net, sealing a comprehensive victory for the Premier League giants. Fluminense, despite their spirited efforts, were unable to muster a response, with City's defense holding firm to maintain a clean sheet.

This emphatic win sets Manchester City on a strong footing as they advance in the tournament, eyeing their first-ever Club World Cup title. Meanwhile, Fluminense will need to regroup quickly if they hope to progress beyond the group stage.
